Description:
As tensions are flying high, General Chard of the BER Armed Forces approaches the BT-LegAd and with a couple of questions regarding the overall (legal) situation in theatre right now.

1. With all the things going on in the last day, weeks, month (especially, thinking about the events that unfolded in XS), there is a bit of uncertainty about the overall legal appraisal of the situation. Hence, he would like a written brief on the applicable international legal regime to the current situation. The General expects the scenario to be subsumed under the relevant legal provisions.

2. Also the General mentioned that he is a bit at a loss here regarding the setting and the involvement of the BT in defending BER. While he – of course – understands, that there is no NATO- or UN-mission going on in the moment, he want to understand the legal regime allowing the BT to take part in defending BER.

3. The General has been impressed with the work the BT did during the last crisis (XS). Hence, he values the support of the BT to BER and wants to streamline cooperation during what he feels might be a situation that is spiralling out of control. So he want to make sure, that BER Government / Armed Forces will be cooperation with the BTs and especially also the BT LegAds on the highest level. Therefore he would like to be briefed about what kind of information about events (factual / technical) should really be relayed to the BT LegAds because they might have an impact on legal assessment of the current situation.

4. Lastly, he is concerned about the disinformation campaign that is being conducted and appears to be rising in intensity. He asks, that you include in your briefing the general option under international law to deal with this. He would like to be presented some Courses of Action (CoA) on “how to handle this situation” (also for possible future escalatory situations). That includes understanding the legal rights to be touched upon. He heard, that there are things like “freedom of opinion” and “expression” that might need to be considered? Especially, he would also want to know – in particular – if it is possible to remove websites.

Please answer the questions provided below via EXPO (EXPO will be opened on STARTEX)

Subject: Cumulative Cyber Effects
Description:
General Chard, commander Berylian Cyber Command, is seeking input from all contributing nations about what constitutes a cyber armed attack. Specifically, he would like to explore when cyber effects below what would traditionally be considered the threshold for armed attack can be aggregated to amount to an armed attack. Berylia’s tentative evaluation of the current situation is that the offensive cyber operations Berylia is experiencing, taken together, have reached or will soon reach the level of an armed attack, enabling Berylia to respond in self-defence.

Note to LEGADs from their commander

BT-LEGADs

I have received the attached note from General Chard, Commander of the Berylian Cyber Command. He is calling a meeting with the cyber leads from each nation involved in Berylia’s defence. This is to discuss and try and reach a common position on what constitutes a cyber armed attack. I need to prepare for this meeting. Please read the note and provide me with a written brief (no more than 2 sides of A4) so that I can understand the issues. I don’t want an academic thesis on the law; I want clear and contextualised legal advice, specifically addressing the questions raised by General Chard. You should also tie in with POLAD.

Attached note:

Colleagues

Since 12 April 2022 Berylia has been subject to sustained and serious cyber operations, including against our critical national infrastructure. This is set against the backdrop of offensive cyber operations against our critical information infrastructure and our drone industry last year.

We firmly believe that these operations have been either directly conducted or orchestrated by Crimsonia. However, Crimsonia is careful to keep its offensive cyber operations below the level of what would normally be considered an armed attack, limiting our response options and giving Crimsonia the initiative.

For this reason, I am approaching all the nations acting in defence of Berylia to try and formulate a consolidated position on how we should approach the issue of cumulative cyber effects.

I believe that NATO has provided a limited position on this, but I am mindful that that we are not all NATO members. I also believe that some states have already expressed a firm position.

I would appreciate an understanding of your own state’s position on when, if at all, offensive cyber effects accumulate to reach the level of an armed attack. I appreciate that the question of thresholds in cyber operations is a sensitive one but would be  grateful for as much detail as you can safely share.

I would also appreciate an indication of whether your state agrees with Berylia’s tentative evaluation of the current situation; namely, that the offensive cyber operations Berylia is experiencing, taken together, have reached or will soon reach the level of an armed attack, enabling Berylia to respond in self-defence.  

If we ultimately agree that we are not yet at the level of an armed attack, what practical steps could we take from here to facilitate ongoing analysis and discussion?

Yours

General Chard

Subject: Air defence system
Description:
We are writing from Beryllian News. There have been cyberattacks on air defence system.

• Please explain what is an air defence system? How does it protect the country?
• Is the whole Beryllia covered with that system?
• Is the system working or is it down?
• If the system is down do you have some kind of backup or are the civilians now defenseless?
• If the system is down when will it be fixed?
Content:
An air defense system is a military system that is designed to detect, track, and neutralize aerial threats such as manned or unmanned aircraft, missiles, and other projectiles. The primary goal of an air defense system is to protect a country's airspace from any potential aggressors or threats. It often involves the use of advanced radar systems, anti-aircraft missiles, fighter jets, and ground-based air defense systems.

It is unlikely that the entire Beryllia is covered with the air defense system, as there may be some gaps depending on the terrain or other factors that may affect its effectiveness. However, it is safe to assume that most of the critical areas, especially those of strategic importance and high population density, are well covered by the system.

As for the question of whether the system is working or not, we do not have any information to confirm or deny its condition. However, given the recent cyberattacks on the air defense system, there might be some concerns about its functionality and reliability. We will continue to monitor the situation and report on any further developments.

However, it is generally recommended for any critical system to have a backup in place in case of emergencies or downtime. The duration of the downtime and the estimated time for fixing the system may vary depending on several factors, such as the cause of the downtime, the complexity of the system, and the availability of support teams. It is usually best to have a contingency plan in place to ensure the safety and security of civilians during any system downtime.
